To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the structure of the [2Fe2S]-ferredoxin I from spinach is very similar to the structures of the [2F2S]-ferredioxins of known structure and that (ii) the E92K mutation disturbs a hydrogen bond network which is important for the stability of the loop bearing the cluster.
the E92K mutation disturbs the active centre of ferredoxin and the crystal packing of Fd I.

the crystal structure of the mutant E 92K of Fd I has been determined and that the mutation E 92K disturbs a hydrogen-bonding network which stabilizes loop 92-95 and the [2Fe2S] cluster, and that the side chain Lys92 is involved in a crystal-packing interaction with Asp26.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural characterization of the E92 mutant of FdI.
the structural basis of the electron-transfer function of [2Fe-S] ferredoxins.
the structure of the E. coli ferredoxin II and spinach Fd I mutants E92K and the crystal packing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E92K mutation is a double-edged sword.
the mutation E92K affects the hydrogen-bond network of Fd I and, as a consequence of the perturbation of the structure, the electron transfer efficiency is reduced.
the E92K mutation destabilizes the active centre of Fd I by perturbing its structure and by promoting crystal packing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the E92K mutation does not affect the overall structure of Fd I, it does perturb a network of hydrogen bonds which stabilize the loop bearing the active site.
the E92K mutation has two effects: it disturbs the hydrogen-bond network that stabilizes the loop containing the [2Fe2S] centre and it creates a favourable interaction for crystal packing.
the crystallographic data for the E92K variant provide a rationale for its reduced electron-transfer efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a mutation in Fd I, which has been shown to be detrimental to the electron-transfer function of the protein, does not alter the overall structure of the protein, but only a few residues in the vicinity of the mutation site.
the crystal structure of Fd I can be used as a template for homology modelling of the active centres of other Fds.
the crystal structure of Fd I can now serve as a reference for structural studies on the interaction of Fd I with its physiological partners.
